slides.title: If an application goes quiet after renter intent is high,
slides.body: A sent application is not a completed application. The goal is a guided recovery path that keeps qualified renters moving instead of fading into incomplete records.
slides.footer: Swipe for the 6 rules behind a cleaner application recovery map

slides.title: The workflow should know exactly where the application stopped without waiting for manual review.
slides.body: Start, partial save, missing ID, income doc gap, screening hold, or unsigned terms should generate a clear stall state so recovery begins while intent is still warm.
slides.footer: Goal: detect the exact drop-off point fast

slides.title: Every stalled application needs one clear next step, not a generic reminder blast.
slides.body: The message should name the missing step, explain how to finish it, and offer the fastest completion path by text, call, or portal link.
slides.footer: Goal: one reminder, one task, one path forward

slides.title: The system should separate technical friction from qualification friction before the team guesses.
slides.body: Portal issues, document confusion, co-applicant delays, screening questions, or price shock should route into different recovery branches and owner queues.
slides.footer: Goal: different blockers trigger different plays

slides.title: High-intent applicants should escalate to a person before they restart the search.
slides.body: If the renter toured, replied, or asked for help, the workflow should route the case to one named leasing owner with the full timeline attached.
slides.footer: Goal: warm applications never sit unowned

slides.title: Recovery should use timing rules that create momentum without dragging dead files forever.
slides.body: Set a short follow-up ladder, reopen windows for good fits, and close cold records cleanly so the team can focus on renters who are still moving.
slides.footer: Goal: urgency for live deals, clean closeout for dead ones

slides.title: Every application outcome should land in the CRM before the next follow-up fires.
slides.body: Missing step, last contact, next owner, completion risk, and closeout reason should write back into the system so reporting and follow-up stay accurate.
slides.footer: Goal: one record shows what is blocked and who owns it
